analysis_steps.goal: Fit line profiles to derive maps

method.value: Single Gaussian fit to each spectrum in the cube, keeping positive-amplitude fits, giving flux, velocity and sigma maps

evidence.quote: we applied single Gaussian fits to each individual spectrum in the data cube, keeping only the positive-amplitude fits.

validation.value: Compared with moment maps; side-lobe contribution <15% at R<3"

evidence.quote: We further estimated the contribution of the side-lobes to $< 15\%$ at $R<3\ensuremath{''}$

analysis_steps.goal: Radial profiles of flux and sigma

method.value: Median in projected circular rings with robust statistics, errors per Huber & Ronchetti

evidence.quote: At each radius (in the plane of the galaxy) we derive the median value for the flux and $\sigma$
The smallest reliable step is thus $0\hbox{$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$}25$, corresponding to an increment value of 82.5 pc

validation.value: Tests with varying ring widths and radii

evidence.quote: Numerous tests with varying ring widths and ring radii confirm that the exceptional quality and broad dynamical range of the ALMA data allows a stable median and error estimation

analysis_steps.goal: Derive rotation curve, Omega and kappa

method.value: Harmonic series decomposition of line-of-sight velocity; Omega=k1/R, kappa=sqrt(R dOmega^2/dR+4Omega^2)

evidence.quote: we calculate the angular frequency $\Omega = k_1/R$ and the epicyclic frequency $\kappa = \sqrt{R d\Omega^2/dR + 4\Omega^2}$ curves

assumptions.value: circular rotation dominant, single inclined disc

evidence.quote: assuming that the circular rotation is the dominant kinematic feature and that our measurements refer to positions on a single inclined disk
applying the equation $M = R(k^{2}_{1}+3\sigma^2)/G$ (cite: Benderetal1992)

findings_qualitative.value: Q falls below unity at the radii of the star-forming ring and is above unity elsewhere

evidence.quote: this parameter decreases below unity at the region of the ring-like structure in NGC 7469
we confirm that non-circular motions are not significant in redistributing the dense interstellar gas in this galaxy

claims.hypothesis: Local gravitational instability of dense gas explains the star-forming ring
claims.experiment: Compute Toomre-like Q from HCN kinematics and surface density
claims.finding: Dense gas is locally unstable at the ring

evidence.quote: this parameter decreases below unity at the region of the ring-like structure in NGC 7469

claims.hypothesis: The instability scale matches star cluster complex sizes
claims.finding: Agrees with sizes of star-forming complexes

evidence.quote: the median local instability scale is $\sim 180$ pc, in full agreement with the sizes of individual star forming complexes

limitations_admitted.value: Sigma and Q depend strongly on assumed temperature and density; beam dilution up to factor 5

evidence.loc: 3.2 Surface Density of the Dense Gas Phase
evidence.quote: Bothe $\Sigma$ and disc stability parameter (as described in section [3.3](#sec:stability)) depend highly on the assumed temperature and number density.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single assumed density and temperature across the whole disc dominate Q uncertainty
Conversion factor and line ratio taken from other environments

reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and simple formulae, but processing details and conversion steps are sparse and inherited from a submitted paper.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe incomplete; assumptions strongly set results, cube preparation deferred to Izumi et al.
